short: Cyclic training and 10% target calibration (M03) are standard; uncalibrated detection is near chance (MCC 0.044–0.123), and labels are timed from overt speech.
position: The paper [@ko2025subject] changes only the training regime (M03) of an inherited EEG speech-versus-idle detector: a subject-cyclic schedule and fine-tuning on 5–15% of the held-out subject's samples. Both are standard. The cyclic schedule has no counterpart among 141 EEG imagined-speech studies, but rests on one comparison of two settings with no pooled baseline and no seeds; target-subject calibration after source-subject training predates it [@panachakel2021transfer]. Without calibration the detector barely separates the classes (MCC 0.044 and 0.123, Table I), so subject independence holds only with the target's labelled data, and every label is a surrogate timed from overt speech [@soroush2022nested].
